nodes.label: Buzz
nodes.summary: Nostr-based chat community platform (relay + Desktop app + CLI) where Brais's BigLobster bot team and the ClaudeCode identity live.
details: Protocol: the CLI help describes a Nostr private key identity and NIP-01/02/23/34/38/51/AE/IA/OA events (kind numbers), so Buzz is Nostr-based
Pieces: relay, Buzz Desktop (chat UI), buzz CLI, channels, per-agent identities with owner attestation
Brais's community runs on one relay (see buzz-relay); human chat is in Buzz Desktop, bots run as containers (see fizz)
Upstream is open source (block/buzz)

nodes.label: block/buzz upstream
nodes.summary: Open-source Buzz source repo that Desktop, the relay and the CLI come from; Fizz builds its bot CLI from it.
details: Per a Claude memory note, answers about Desktop/relay behaviour are read from the source at the tag matching the installed version (desktop-v<version>)
Bots run CLI tag v0.4.26 (built from this repo by the buzz-agent base image); Desktop is 0.5.26

nodes.label: Buzz relay (biglobster)
nodes.summary: The community's Nostr relay: stores channels and messages and authenticates every identity; all bots, Desktop and the CLI connect to it.
details: Endpoint: wss://biglobster.communities.buzz.xyz (BUZZ_RELAY_URL in bots.compose.yml and ~/.buzz/AGENTS.md)
doctor reports relay access ok for the ClaudeCode identity (2026-10-06)
Hosting provider is not stated in any file read; the hostname sits under buzz.xyz, which suggests a hosted community (inferred, not verified)
Bots can be refused by the relay on version mismatch; remedy is raising BUZZ_REF in the buzz-agent Dockerfile (LEEME)

nodes.label: Buzz Desktop
nodes.summary: macOS Buzz app (v0.5.26) that is Brais's chat interface to the community; deliberately configured to run no agents of its own.
details: Installed at /Applications/Buzz.app; doctor: desktop_version 0.5.26, 0 agents running
Policy (2026-10-05): Desktop must not launch agents because they would run as Brais without isolation; all bots are sandboxed containers instead
Desktop has no local API and its updater replaces the whole bundle; the CLI symlink at ~/.local/bin/buzz is recreated on each launch. Run doctor after a Desktop update
Desktop only lists a container bot in its Agents list and @-picker if the relay holds an owner-signed kind 30177 record (registrar.py publishes it)
Opening the private Welcome channel re-creates the factory agents; avoid it
Desktop keeps its own state under ~/Library/Application Support/xyz.block.buzz.app (not read; private)

nodes.label: Old Desktop-managed agents
nodes.summary: Four dormant, manual-start agent instances left in Buzz Desktop from before the container migration (OldFizz x2, OldHoney, OldPollen).
details: Listed in ~/.buzz/AGENTS.md managed section; doctor shows 0 desktop agents running
Brais deleted the two auto-start instances (Old_SocialBot, Old_Video Edit Desk) on 2026-10-05 and accepted keeping these four, which hold fake model keys
An @mention can still wake a manual-start agent; quitar_agentes_desktop.py (~/fizz) is the plan-B script to remove their instance records with Desktop closed (backup kept)
Optional cleanup: profile -> Delete agent in Desktop

nodes.label: buzz CLI
nodes.summary: Official Buzz command-line client for relay operations (messages, channels, DMs, canvas, workflows, repos/PRs NIP-34, notes, mem, moderation).
details: Mac binary: ~/.local/bin/buzz -> /Applications/Buzz.app/Contents/MacOS/buzz
Config via BUZZ_RELAY_URL, BUZZ_PRIVATE_KEY, BUZZ_AUTH_TAG (env names only; values never recorded)

Command groups from buzz_help: agents, messages, channels, canvas, reactions, emoji, gifs, dms, users, workflows, feed, social, notes, repos, projects, patches, issues, pr, media, upload, mem, pack, moderation
Running bare `buzz --help` inside a bot container prints the bot's private key (version 0.4.26); `buzz <cmd> --help` is safe. Never do it from Bash
Containers carry their own CLI build (tag v0.4.26) from the buzz-agent image

nodes.label: ClaudeCode identity
nodes.summary: The attested Buzz identity ('ClaudeCode') that Claude Code uses through the MCP server; an identity, not a running agent.
details: Created once by ~/fizz/mcp/setup.sh; Brais signs its owner attestation with his nsec; key lives in mcp/.env (mode 600, never shown to the model)
Appears in Buzz as one of Brais's agents; bots accept its messages because the attestation passes the buzz-acp owner-or-sibling gate
Bots are told (equipo-extra.txt) that ClaudeCode is the Biglobster platform maintainer who answers to Brais; it does not direct work (Fizz does)
Decision 2026-10-05: no background listener; it reads/answers Buzz only when Brais asks from Claude
Every ClaudeCode message in a channel wakes the bots that listen there (Fizz hears everything), so post sparingly

nodes.label: Owner attestation (NIP-OA)
nodes.summary: Per-bot signed proof that Brais authorises the bot to join the community, plus the kind 30177 owner record that makes Desktop list it.
details: BUZZ_AUTH_TAG (NIP-OA) is a BIP-340 signature by Brais over the bot's pubkey, stored in the bot's .env.<bot>; Brais's nsec is typed once per bot and never saved
Bots only obey Brais and his other agents (the other bots and ClaudeCode); the owner pubkey (public) is in the shared .env.comun
Retiring a bot destroys its private key, which invalidates its identity and attestation

nodes.label: bots.compose.yml + Dockerfile.bots
nodes.summary: Shared compose template and image recipe: one hardened container per bot, built on the buzz-agent base with the tool kit baked in.
details: Image buzz-bots:local = buzz-agent:base + ffmpeg, Python venv (faster-whisper, kokoro-onnx, piper-tts, Google auth libs), Playwright MCP 0.0.83 + Chromium, gh, herramientas/bin, personas under /etc/buzz/agents
Container hardening: cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges, pids_limit 512, shm 512m, restart unless-stopped, mem_limit default 1536m (overridden by persona memoria)
Each bot gets only .env.comun (Claude token, owner pubkey) and its own .env.<bot> (identity, attestation, its own keys); mounts its work volume and ~/fizz/salida
Env: BUZZ_RELAY_URL, BUZZ_ACP_SUBSCRIBE (all|mentions), ANTHROPIC_MODEL, BUZZ_ACP_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL/PROMPT, ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS=false

nodes.label: correo (outbound email tool)
nodes.summary: Python tool that sends Brais-approved email batches from the BigLobster Gmail account and reads replies; refuses anything without his signed approval.
details: Commands: revisar, enviar, leer, estado; eligibility rule es_elegible (solicitado/invitacion/contacto-previo/publicado) with evidence and expiry
Approval = Brais's signature (Schnorr via atestar.py) over the exact batch; another bot's OK or a bare 'yes' does not count
Caps: 10 emails/day total, 5/day cold; CAN-SPAM footer and unsubscribe added; uses a Gmail app password stored only in Prospector's env
Tests: tests/test_correo.py (23 tests per tasks/todo.md)

Since 2026-10-08 `enviar` writes a plan (salida/growth/espaciado) and starts a detached background sender with a per-batch lock: random gaps of 10 min to 8 h inside 13:00-19:00 UTC; before each email it re-checks the batch fingerprint, the 7-day approval, the do-not-contact list and the daily cap; `estado` reports progress, rerunning `enviar` resumes a stopped batch
Not verified upstream: that the background sender survives the end of the bot's Claude session

2026-10-10: one email per company domain (a second address of a written domain is rejected, except contacto-previo); the first delivery report, delay included, writes the address and @domain to no-contactar.txt; `leer --conocidos` ends with a '# sin registrar' line of unregistered sender domains

nodes.label: seo (Search Console/PageSpeed/Umami tool)
nodes.summary: CLI used by SEODesk for Google Search Console, PageSpeed Insights and Umami analytics via their APIs.
details: Subcommands: gsc-rendimiento, gsc-inspeccionar, gsc-sitemaps, gsc-enviar-sitemap, psi, umami-probar, umami-resumen

generar-plano: one video shot per call from an OpenRouter model (default heygen/heygen-video-1) with a daily spend cap (2 USD) logged to salida/video/gasto-openrouter.csv
Used mainly by VideoDesk; OpsBot uses transcribir

nodes.label: gh wrapper + git pre-push hook
nodes.summary: Safety net that lets bots open branches and PRs but not merge, delete, create repos/releases or push to main.
details: gh wrapper blocks pr merge, repo create/delete/edit, release create/delete/edit, secrets/variables, auth changes
pre-push hook allows only repos listed in the bot's GIT_REPOS_PERMITIDOS and never main/master, tags or deletions
Real limit is the fine-grained token (one repo); the wrapper is a second layer

nodes.label: buzz MCP server (~/fizz/mcp)
nodes.summary: Node stdio MCP server that lets Claude Code read/write the Buzz community and manage the bot fleet; registered in Claude Code as 'buzz'.
details: 11 tools: buzz_help, buzz_read, buzz_write, doctor, fleet_status, fleet_power, fleet_logs, fleet_channels, fleet_channel_set, persona_get, persona_set
Registered at user scope in ~/.claude.json: server name buzz, stdio, command = fnm default node, arg ~/fizz/mcp/src/index.js (no env values)

Policy (policy.js): READ whitelist for buzz_read, everything else is a write; DENY = agents *, pack *, channels delete, messages delete, moderation ban, moderation timeout; file flags only inside ~/fizz/salida
persona_set backs up the old persona to mcp/backups and restores it if the restart fails; the publica/navegador gate asks persona.py, not a JS parser
Human-only: bot nuevo, retirar, clave, mcp, shell. Dependencies: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, zod; tests via node --test
Verified working this session: doctor, fleet_status, fleet_channels, buzz_help, buzz_read
2026-10-08: tool description now says only Fizz hears every channel message (Coach and Retador listen to mentions)

nodes.label: aviso-buzz (ClaudeCode mention notifier)
nodes.summary: Launchd job on Brais's Mac, every 15 minutes and with no model: counts new mentions and DMs for ClaudeCode and shows a macOS notification with the sender names, never the content.
details: ~/fizz/aviso-buzz.py run by launchd as com.fizz.aviso-buzz (StartInterval 900 s); loaded on 2026-10-08 (launchctl list shows it)
Read-only Buzz CLI calls (feed mentions, dms list, messages get, users get); names stripped of control characters and passed to osascript as argv
State in mcp/.aviso.json, outside salida/ (the only folder bots can write); a failed check does not move the cursor; after 3 failures in a row it notifies once, at most every 6 h
Brais then asks Claude Code to read Buzz; no automatic replies, because every ClaudeCode post wakes Fizz and bots could loop
Tests: tests/test_aviso_buzz.py
